text:
incident-bot: Heads-up: scheduled rolling cache compaction in us-west1 on 2025-11-12 02:00-03:00 UTC. Expected duration ~60m. Potential short-lived latency spikes for embeddings and small text-gen requests. Pager primary: @Nora P. Secondary: @Owen L. Posting statuspage copy below and ops checklist.

Maya T.: What exactly are we compacting and why might latency spike?

Owen L.: We're running a KV compaction to reclaim fragmented on-GPU cache shards after the last model swap. Compaction pauses servicing for small windows per shard; autoscaling covers throughput but tail latency can spike ~100-400ms for affected shards. No token loss.

Sara K.: Draft status page copy looks good, slight wording tweak to avoid "degraded" -> use "temporary latency increase". Also include guidance for customers about retries/backoff.

incident-bot: Statuspage draft (to be posted at T-30m unless changed):

```
Status: Scheduled Maintenance
Service: inference.redwood.com (us-west1) — KV cache compaction
Start: 2025-11-12T02:00Z
Expected duration: ~60 minutes
Impact: Some requests (notably embedding calls and small generation requests) may experience temporary latency increases of ~100-400ms during shard compaction. Throughput and request correctness unaffected.
Customer guidance: Implement short retry/backoff for 5xx and 429s; consider brief client-side timeout extension during window.
```

Diego R.: Suggested customer email snippet: "We’ll run a maintenance job in us-west1 on Nov 12 02:00 UTC to compact inference caches. You may see brief latency increases; no data loss expected. If you rely on strict p95 latency, consider routing to another region during the window."

Maya T.: Can we include a fallback policy — auto-failover to cheaper model variant if latency exceeds threshold?

Owen L.: Yes — we have a policy in the router: if p95 latency > 750ms for 2 consecutive 5m buckets, route new requests to model-x-small in other region. I'll wire that rule and attach the feature flag name: router.compact_fallback.v1.

Nora P.: I'll be primary pager. Runbook excerpt:

```
1) Check alert channel: #pager-us-west1 and /alerts
2) Look at per-route latency: https://console/redwood/latency?region=us-west1
3) If tail > 750ms for >5m: enable fallback:
   curl -X POST https://api.redwood.local/admin/route/fallback -d '{"policy":"router.compact_fallback.v1","enable":true}'
4) To pause compaction gracefully: ssh ops@compactionctl 'pause-shard <shard-id>'
5) If we see >5% error rate or sustained >3m outage: escalate to eng-sre and initiate rollback plan.
```

Sara K.: I'll add the customer guidance text to the announcement and shorten the engineering wording for external copy.

Diego R.: Who will publish the statuspage at T-30? I can do it at T-20 if needed.

Owen L.: I'll create the scheduled incident entry now and set the automated update at T-30. Diego, please push the customer email at T-60 and drop a link here when queued.

Nora P.: Oncall handoff: I'll take primary from 01:45-03:30 UTC. @Owen L. you'll be backup and monitoring the fallback triggers. If I'm paged and can't ack within 2m, incident-bot will escalate to Owen.

Maya T.: Rollback plan quick check — if fallback causes correctness regressions, what's the window to revert?

Owen L.: Revert fallback with same API call (enable=false). We expect <5m to revert routing globally. If model correctness issues appear, we'll pause compaction (pause-shard) and revert routing. Documented in runbook section 5.

incident-bot: Reminder scheduled: statuspage will auto-post at 1758003632 (T-30m). A manual update can be posted if changes occur. :bell:

Nora P.: Thanks everyone — I'll be online and will post a short post-mortem if anything unexpected happens. :white_check_mark:
